subject: Integration action plan: SDK bootstrap, auth & local test plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration action plan: SDK bootstrap, auth & local test plan

Hi Samir — great conversation this morning. Quick recap + proposed action items so we’re aligned on scope for the POC and what the engineering ramp looks like. I’ve attached a small quickstart repo and an integration checklist we can iterate on.

Summary of your goals
- Server-side TypeScript inference for product search + semantic reranking
- Low-latency embedding lookups; offline index + nearline reranker
- SAML/OIDC for auth, minimal token exposure, audit logs required

Technical notes / decisions to confirm
1) SDKs: we recommend the TypeScript SDK for your node backend (serverless or container). Python examples included for batch embedding jobs.
2) Auth: two viable options:
   - OIDC (recommended): single sign-on + short-lived tokens; maps to your existing IdP.
   - API keys with mTLS for service-to-service if you prefer not to wire OIDC initially.
3) Routing / deployment mode: start hosted API for quick validation (fastest onboarding). If throughput stabilizes, we’ll move to a Dedicated pool in us-west for consistent latency.
4) Structured output / tool-calling: for now we’ll use JSON schema + function-calling in the SDK; we’ll iterate on safe parsing rules for search result enrichments.
5) Embeddings & reranker: sample flow in the repo includes a local FAISS server for dev and an example reranker that scores candidate snippets with a lightweight transformer.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Samir: confirm TypeScript + IdP details (issuer, client_id) — by EOD Mon 3/8
- Redwood (Karthik): provision trial hosted keys + OIDC test config; upload quickstart and checklist — by Fri 3/6 (attached)
- Redwood (Ben/CS): prepare Dedicated sizing guidance and trial credits if needed — by Tue 3/9
- Acme Eng (Priya): validate local dev constraints (network egress, allowed containers) and share any firewall rules — by Mon 3/8

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart-2026.zip (TS + Py examples, readme), integration-checklist-ACME.xlsx (environment + security gating checklist).

Next step: 30-minute engineering sync next week to walk the repo and sketch the minimal POC. Please reply with your preferred times.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.ai]

Thanks Karthik — useful recap. A few quick notes from our side:
- We’ll prioritize TypeScript (serverless on Vercel for the API layer).
- OIDC is preferred; I’ll pull issuer and client_id from our SSO team and share by Monday.
- For local dev we need a plain Docker option (no internet egress during testing for some teams) — can the quickstart run entirely offline with sample embeddings?

Also can you share a simple architecture diagram that shows: hosted API vs Dedicated, where embeddings live (managed vs self-hosted), and the reranker step? Priya will be on the call for the POC; I’ve looped her in.

Samir
